title: Why CD Lasers Use Infrared Light

scenes.text: The 1982 CD player that read discs with a 780 nm laser
Many believe CDs use a visible red laser like DVDs.
scenes.label: CD uses red laser

scenes.text: CDs actually use an infrared laser around 780 nm because it reads the longer pits more reliably.
scenes.label: Infrared laser reads pits

scenes.text: Infrared lets CDs store up to 700 MB without error.
scenes.label: Infrared = capacity
scenes.sub: The longer wavelength improves data density and error tolerance.
